mia (eng-ml): kicking off an FP8 kernel handshake probe on H100/L40S for atlas13b-rc. doing shadow traffic + a 10% canary on dedicated pool. initial warmup looks fine but tail latency variance spikes during long-prefix workloads. attaching logs below.

sam (eng-runtime): noted — we've seen autobatch handshake increase queue depth before. can you paste the canary config?

mia (eng-ml): 
```yaml
kernel_enable: fp8
canary: 0.10
autobatch:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_concurrent: 32
fallback_policy: [\"int8\", \"fp16\"]
run_mode: shadow
```

olga (eng-ml): two observations from smoke: 1) fallback to fp16 triggered even when latency SLOs were met, 2) KV-cache reuse counters show occasional evictions at ~seq_len 1800. might be tiling handshake mismatch.

kevin (eng-sre): infra saw GPU temp spikes correlated with those eviction windows on L40S nodes. raised a thermal alert and throttled burst for one pool. tagging incident: #thermal-spike-440.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused at 11:12 UTC due to autoscale event; run: https://ci.internal/runs/98321 (paused by autoscaler).

tess (product): user impact? any quality regressions on eval sets or customer-facing deltas?

mia (eng-ml): accuracy on our validation sweep (commons/qa + summarization slices) is stable: delta <0.1% vs baseline. but for longprefix tests (prefix >1500 tokens) we see token-level drift in the last 50 tokens on ~0.5% of samples. example diff below (orig vs fp8-handshake):

--- sample 42 ---
orig: "...the committee concluded the proposal would benefit from further review before adoption."
fp8-handshake: "...the committee suggested additional review before any formal adoption."

(minor paraphrase, but can alter downstream extraction heuristics)

sam (eng-runtime): logs show entries like `tile_mismatch: true` and `kv_eviction=1` around the same timestamps. that implies the tiling handshake can lose alignment when autobatch merges variable-length prefixed requests. quant round-trip can amplify small numeric diffs.

olga (eng-ml): repro steps I used: run the harness with --prefix-len 1800 --batch 4 --seed 1234 against canary image. quick script: 
```bash
python eval_harness.py --model atlas13b-rc --quant fp8 --prefix-len 1800 --batch-size 4 --canary true --seed 1234
```
I can push the exact traces to the stash.

mia (eng-ml): proposed mitigation plan: 
1) temporarily disable autobatch handshake for L40S longseq traffic (prefix > 1024)
2) enable deterministic tiling path in runtime for FP8 codepath to preserve KV alignment
3) extend shadow to 20% and run A/B with longer sampling window (72h)
4) add an automatic rollback trigger if token-drift exceed threshold (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE drop >0.5 on slice)

kevin (eng-sre): will add autoscale override and thermal cap for that fleet; also will collect perf counters (tile_mismatch_count, kv_eviction_count, mean_gpu_temp) every 30s.

sam (eng-runtime): I'll prototype a deterministic-tiling toggle behind a runtime flag and add extra checks during handshake to refuse batch welds that would misalign KV offsets. rough patch ETA EOD.

olga (eng-ml): I'll expand the eval slice to cover prefix-length distribution from production logs and run sensitivity ablations for quantized kernels (fp8 vs awq/gptq).

mia (eng-ml): follow-ups: @sam runtime patch + feature flag, @kevin infra caps + metrics, @olga expanded eval harness. I'll open a canary issue and attach these repro traces.

sam (eng-runtime): sounds good. if deterministic tiling fixes alignment we can re-enable autobatch handshake with a gradual ramp.

kevin (eng-sre): putting a temporary scaling policy: max_burst_nodes=2, thermal_cap=80C for L40S canary pool. monitor dashboard updated.

mia (eng-ml): thanks — tagging this thread with #fp8-bakeoff #longseq #handshake. will report back with A/B results. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Issue created: INF-5623 "FP8 handshake: tiling mismatch + longprefix token drift" (assignee: mia)

mia (eng-ml): assigning and scheduling follow-up meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review 24h shadow metrics.

tess (product): please include potential customer visible mitigation text in the notes (we may need to notify a small set of early adopters).

mia (eng-ml): will draft an internal blurb and a targeted customer note if drift is reproducible at >1% of queries.

olga (eng-ml): uploading traces now.

kevin (eng-sre): monitoring hooks added.

mia (eng-ml): end of thread for now.
